**Solution 2** is the most likely to be correct.

**Direction of the divergence.** With the Type I error fixed at most ε under H₀, the Stein-type Type II exponent is D(P₀‖P₁), with H₀ in the first slot. Solution 1 uses D(11/36 ‖ 5/12), which reverses the roles. Solution 2 uses D(5/12 ‖ 11/36), which has the correct orientation.

**Consistency of the test channel.** The rate matches the Wyner-Ziv design exactly. With X = U ⊕ Z, Z ~ Bern(1/4), and U ~ Bern(1/2), we get I(U;X) = 1 − h₂(1/4) and, under H₀, I(U;Y) = 1 − h₂(5/12). So I(U;X|Y) = h₂(5/12) − h₂(1/4) = R. The posterior values P₀(Y=1|U) = 5/12 and P₁(Y=1|U) = 11/36 are also right, since (1/4)(2/3) + (3/4)(1/3) = 5/12 and (1/4)(8/9) + (3/4)(1/9) = 11/36.

**Value check.** The log-form in Solution 2 expands correctly to log₂3 − (3/4)log₂5 + (7/12)log₂7 − (5/12)log₂11 ≈ 0.03971. Solution 1's expression evaluates to ≈ 0.03796, which is the reversed divergence.

**Caveats.** Solution 2's converse is hand-waved; it invokes Mrs. Gerber's lemma loosely and asserts the maximizing U without proof. Its achievability also relies on heuristic concentration arguments. The true ε→0 exponent for this distributed setting may involve a min-max characterization, so D(5/12 ‖ 11/36) is the most plausible answer among the three rather than a verified one. Solution 3's D(5/12 ‖ 1/4) has no justification from the problem's structure and is not supported.

CHOICE: 2
